I sent round-2 lanes B, C, D and F back with directions. D's kill (`f88344fef43ce018`) is accepted, and the rest go back as follows:
- **F, `is_include_statement`:** this item is really dead code. The C++ producer always strips leading whitespace from include lines before this function sees them, so its own whitespace handling can never matter. The child will delete it and add a `debug_assert` stating the assumption, instead of recording NOT CAUGHT.
- **The four unresolved items:** each now has a concrete lead.
  - B: a C++ out-of-line member whose qualified name crosses a line break.
  - C, first item: write the test through the anchor-miss diagnostic path, the only path that reaches the function.
  - C, second item: a C++ header declaration whose definition is in a `.cpp` file, so the canonical identity differs from the physical one.
  - D: assert the family-selector output directly, rather than a source count.

**Elsewhere:**
- #8718 (the #8699 fix) is in merge batch #8733.
- Round-2 children for t2 lanes A and E are still working.
- The combined t4/t5 run (T45) is running on H2.

Round-2 lane A for t2 is done (`e0d4caec85`), with all four items resolved:
- **Two kills:** the two batch tests now call the public navigation functions on a real analyzer. Each fails with its truncation mutant and passes once the mutant is reverted.
- **Two NOT CAUGHT,** both for structural reasons I checked:
  - Valid Java never yields a field access over a method-call name, so a kind-ranking mutant cannot change the selected kind.
  - The hook name passed to `language_support_for_hook` appears only in a panic message that cannot be reached, so asking for the "wrong" hook returns the same result.

**Still running:**
- **Round-2 t2 lane E:** the child is working on its six sources items.
- **Round-2 t2 lanes B, C, D and F:** the child is applying my follow-up directions.

When these finish, I'll merge the round-2 branches into one follow-up PR.
The trim isn't in the first lines of `symbol_source_candidate_files`. I'll read the exact mutant diff from the round-2 file.

I accepted round-2 lane E for t2. It covered its six items with one kill and five NOT CAUGHT, and the kill fails with the mutant applied and passes once it is reverted.

**Kill (`67bb42e51a`):** `file_outline_reserves_its_first_block` catches its mutant.

**NOT CAUGHT, and why each is left alone:**
- **Redundant trim:** both the resolver and the selector splitter already trim the input, so the extra `trim()` is harmless.
- **Possibly dead fallback:** two mutants show that `resolve_file_anchored_symbol_sources` may only ever run after a lookup has already failed. If so, the fallback is dead code. Deleting it needs a reachability check first, so I recorded it on #8701.
- **Sibling ranges:** the child flagged this item as not proven equivalent in general, so it is open on #8701 too.

**Still running:**

- T45 on H2, the combined t4/t5 verification.

When both finish, the round-2 branches go into one follow-up PR.

#8718 has landed and closed #8699. The usage graph now reports a call through a missing relative import as incomplete, and imports that leave the workspace as a gap of their own. I removed the `agent-in-progress` label from #8699 and deleted its worktree.

All five round-14 PRs are on `master`: #8695, #8706, #8709, #8715 and #8718.

**Still running:**
- the round-2 child for t2 lanes B, C, D and F;

| Lane | Result |

| E | 1 kill, 5 NOT CAUGHT |

The integration branch changes one production file, `summaries.rs` (the deletion and its `debug_assert`), plus four `suite_symbols` test files. Its validation covers fmt, the affected tools tests, all of `suite_symbols`, and clippy.

T45, the combined t4/t5 verification, is still mapping on H2. It started at 02:41Z. Its round-2 results will join the same follow-up PR.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Round 2 kept turning "the test doesn't catch it" into "the code doesn't matter". Three items this round, two last round, ended as dead-code deletions. A surviving mutant often shows that a branch no longer affects the outcome, and deleting the branch fixes that better than another test would.
- Merging round 2 into one follow-up PR from `master` keeps review small: the reviewer sees only the strengthened tests and the deletions, not lane work that already landed.

**H2:** I shut it down. All EC2 verification for this crate is finished, and the results are saved locally.

The t5 C/D round 2 caught all three mutants (`6ad3122b0c`), each proven locally. It changed `git_hotspots.rs` and `maintainability_size.rs`, both of which keep their tests inline, so I'll confirm every hunk is inside a test module.

Every hunk is inside the files' test modules (line 783 onwards in `git_hotspots.rs`, 1222 in `maintainability_size.rs`), so production code is unchanged.

Round 2 for t4 lanes B and C proved none of its seven mutants, and the child left no commit. Two of its findings need checking before I decide anything:
- **The newline prefix:** the child says the status-token newline prefix never appeared in `-z` output. Lane B's earlier fix said that newline is Git's record separator. If the child is right, the strip may be dead code.
- **A C# case:** the child says a same-class C# test was "already missing on baseline". That could be a real missing-tests defect.

I'll read the child's evidence.

Round 2 for t4 lanes B and C ended with none of its seven mutants caught, so it adds nothing to #8746. I recorded all seven on #8701, each with the next input that would settle it.

**The C# case is not a bug.** The fixture put the `[Fact]` test method inside the production file `App/Value.cs`. The analysis rightly did not treat it as a test, so it reported the changed method as untested.

**One item may be dead code.** The child observed that `git log -z --name-status` never puts a newline in front of a status token. That contradicts lane B's earlier comment that this newline is Git's record separator. If the child is right, `strip_git_log_token_prefix` does nothing and should be deleted. Settling it means checking the exact format string relevance passes to Git, so I logged it on #8701 rather than act on it now.

**Round 2 so far:**

| Tranche | Lanes | Result |
|---|---|---|
| t2 | all | in #8746 and approved: 5 kills, 1 deletion, 8 NOT CAUGHT, 2 open |
| t5 | C and D | 3 kills, ready to merge into #8746 |
| t4 | B and C | 0 of 7, all open on #8701 |
| t5 | A and B | 4 items, still running |

When t5 A and B finish, I'll merge both t5 branches into #8746 and send that part for its separate review.

Round 2 for t5 lanes A and B produced one kill and three NOT CAUGHT. The kill is `da3257fe70347eaa`: an uncalled Java constructor now reaches the capped query. The three NOT CAUGHT:
- **A2:** the report clamps the usage cap to one, so the producer returns `TooManyCallsites` before the two-usage comparison is ever reached.
- **A3:** the scoped producer records a status for every requested node, so the `None` arm the mutant changes never runs.
- **B:** `Repository::open` requires the project root to be the repository root, so pointing it at the parent directory changes nothing.

The B finding also suggests a usability gap. A project opened at a subdirectory of a Git repository can't run the secret scan at all, and fails with "requires a JGit-backed repository". The scanner uses `Repository::open` where other Git tools search upward for the repository. I'll file that, then merge both t5 branches into #8746.
Next I'll merge both t5 round-2 branches into #8746's branch, along with the latest `master`.

Round 2 is finished for every tranche. The t5 work is now merged into #8746 (head `2ddc91f53a`) and being validated: the affected tools tests, `suite_smells`, `suite_symbols`, clippy, fmt and classification.

**Round-2 results by tranche:**

| Tranche | Kills | Deletions | NOT CAUGHT | Open (#8701) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| t2 | 5 | 1 | 8 | 2 |
| t4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 7 |
| t5 | 4 | 0 | 3 | 0 |

**New issue #8753.** The secret scan fails for a project opened inside a subdirectory of a Git repository: it calls `Repository::open` where the other Git tools use `discover`. Its own code already tracks repository and project roots separately, so nested projects were evidently meant to work.

**Next:** when validation passes, I'll push #8746 and send the t5 changes for their separate review, then mark it ready.

#8746 now holds all of round 2 (head `2ddc91f53a`), and its validation passed:

- the tools tests for the modules round 2 touched: 124 tests;
- clippy, fmt and open-core classification.

- **Deletion:** 1 piece of dead code removed, in `summaries.rs`.
- **NOT CAUGHT:** 11 items, each with a structural reason.
- **Still open:** 9 items (2 from t2, 7 from t4), tracked on #8701 with the evidence found so far.

When the reviewer approves the t5 part, I'll check `master` once more, merge if needed, and mark #8746 ready. That closes round 14 for the tools crate.
